what: Records a measurement of anything (outline 17.27). Metric(holder_dir, charter_path, source=...).record(name, value, unit=, subject=, start=, end=, info=, at=) writes one record into the holder's data recorder at <holder>/tools/data_recorder/metrics/ — no bus, no database (17.27.1). A name the recording component's charter does not declare under "metrics": {name: {consumer, unit}} raises UndeclaredMetric and nothing is written (17.27.4). take(holder_dir, sink) hands what waits to sink(rows), each row exactly the one table's COLUMNS (at, name, source, start, end, value, unit, subject, info; 17.27.2), and clears them only after the sink returns (17.27.3).
why: Akien, 2026-11-09, outline 17.27: 'a metric is a primitive; its job is to measure whatever it is, and like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer.' Answering Q#78 he ruled that the inference proxy's spent, saved and latency are metrics, not learning, and 'inference tickets are only for debugging' — so the yield report (11.4.4.2) needs one table every source records into the same way.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.metric.metric import Metric, take, COLUMNS, UndeclaredMetric`. No CLI door. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/metric/proofs/test_metric.py`.
entry: FRESH build, 2026-11-10. Stands on cairn/tools/data_recorder (the holder's mailbox) rather than a second store. The table itself is its holder's: the cairn device creates and owns it through db_domain's store until Recovery exists (5.3.6, 6.6.3.4).
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, born at the ticket's BUILDME crossing. The tool's ongoing state (records waiting) lives under each holder in instance-space.
how_it_learns: It does not; it records. Its READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS is a HYPOTHESIS (a day) until the first consumer measures how often a report is asked for.
filed_edges: (a) The declaration is checked at record time, against the charter as it reads then; nothing yet reds a charter that declares a name nothing records.

(b) take clears after the sink returns; a sink that commits and then the process dies before the clear re-hands those rows next time (at-least-once). The table's consumer tolerates a duplicate row; a lost row it could not see.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_metric.py, one tooth per falsifier clause. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a declared name does not land in the holder's metrics recorder with its name, source, value and declared unit, or the tool imports a bus or a database; (2) an undeclared name, or one with a blank consumer, writes anything; (3) take hands rows not exactly COLUMNS, or clears before the sink returns, or clears when the sink raises; (4) the recorder's read frequency is undeclared. WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: a table created here, or a poll.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Akien owns the definition (outline 17.27). CC writes the code and the proofs.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured; a metric is the measurement recorded)
Law 6 (a tool has users; the recorder's state is the holder's)
provenance: Shaped by Akien and CC 2026-11-09 into outline 17.27 (Q#78 answered at 11.4.4.2).
